title: Nordbank — RFP kickoff (Security + Data Residency + Response Plan)
summary: Kickoff call for Nordbank’s RFP covering Redwood Dedicated/Private options. Nordbank outlined timeline (RFP responses due end of Jan), required questionnaires (vendor security questionnaire + SIG Lite/CAIQ-style mapping), and strict EU data residency constraints (processing and storage in EU; log retention boundaries; no cross-region failover without approval). Redwood confirmed what can be answered from standard security collateral vs what requires NDA (SOC 2 report) and agreed on a response plan: Lukas to coordinate RFP submission; Olga to manage evidence request flow and approvals; Fatima/Colin to supply deployment-mode-specific language for Dedicated EU and Private VPC. Identified open questions on SIEM/audit log export format, retention configuration, and subprocessor list/DPA references.
topics: RFP timeline, submission format, and stakeholder map
Required questionnaires and evidence expectations (SOC 2 under NDA)
EU data residency requirements (inference, logs, backups, support access)
Deployment options: Dedicated in EU vs Private VPC, and how to describe shared responsibility
Audit logging, SIEM export, SSO/SCIM/RBAC control statements
Response plan, owners, and review/approval process
next_steps: Redwood to send the latest Enterprise Security FAQ link plus the EU data residency/retention one-pager (customer-facing) by 2026-01-17.
Nordbank to share the full vendor security questionnaire workbook + any required attestations (SIG Lite/CAIQ mapping) by 2026-01-17.
Nordbank Procurement to initiate NDA so Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report via the evidence request process.
Redwood to schedule a 45-min technical deep dive focused on Private VPC + audit log export / SIEM integration next week (target 2026-01-21 or 2026-01-22).
Redwood to confirm the exact EU region(s) Nordbank requires and whether EU-only support personnel is a requirement or preference.
action_items: Lukas Meyer — Send Nordbank the RFP response plan email (owners, dates, list of artifacts) — Due 2026-01-16 EOD
Olga Petrov — Prepare evidence request checklist + NDA template instructions for SOC 2 report request — Due 2026-01-17
Fatima Noor — Draft EU data residency phrasing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (including limitations and no-roadmap language) — Due 2026-01-20
Colin O'Donnell — Provide Private VPC deployment security appendix inputs (networking boundaries, customer-managed controls) — Due 2026-01-20
Anna Bergström — Send Nordbank questionnaire pack and confirm RFP due date/timezone and portal submission instructions — Due 2026-01-17
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcription

Meeting: Nordbank — RFP kickoff (Security + Data Residency + Response Plan)
Date: 2026-01-16
Start time: 10:03 AM CET
Duration: 53 min
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

Attendees
Redwood Inference: Lukas Meyer (AE), Fatima Noor (Solutions Engineering, regulated deployments), Olga Petrov (GRC), Colin O'Donnell (Private deployments)
Nordbank: Anna Bergström (Procurement), Erik Jensen (Security/CISO Office), Marie Keller (IT Risk & Compliance), Tomasz Nowak (Cloud Platform), Sven Richter (Enterprise Architecture)

---
Auto Summary (generated)
- Nordbank RFP requires EU data residency and clear statements on logging, retention, and access controls.
- Redwood will provide standard collateral (Security FAQ, data residency/retention overview) and gated evidence (SOC 2) under NDA.
- Agreed owners and dates; follow-up deep dive on Private VPC + SIEM export.

---
[00:00] Lukas Meyer: Cool. Um, thanks everyone for making time. This is Lukas from Redwood Inference. I’m the account owner on our side. I’ve got Fatima, Olga, and Colin with me.

[00:10] Lukas Meyer: The goal today is pretty simple: align on the RFP timeline, who needs what, and then especially the EU residency constraints and questionnaires so we don’t, you know, waste cycles with back-and-forth.

[00:25] Anna Bergström: Yeah, thanks Lukas. This is Anna from procurement. We’re coordinating the vendor responses. We have security and platform here as well.

[00:33] Erik Jensen: Erik, security side.

[00:35] Marie Keller: Marie, IT risk and compliance.

[00:38] Tomasz Nowak: Tomasz, cloud platform engineering.

[00:41] Sven Richter: Sven, enterprise architecture.

[00:45] Lukas Meyer: Great. Maybe Anna, do you want to start with timeline and deliverables? Like, due date, format, portal, that kind of thing.

[00:55] Anna Bergström: Sure. So we issued the RFP this week. Responses are due end of month, specifically January 31st, 17:00 CET. It’s a portal upload, but we can also accept the workbook plus attachments by email as a backup.

[01:12] Anna Bergström: The RFP pack includes a commercial template, a technical questionnaire, and a security questionnaire. For security, it’s our standard bank vendor security questionnaire. It’s… it’s similar to SIG Lite, but not exactly. We also ask for mapping to ISO 27001 controls, but it’s fine if you answer in narrative.

[01:30] Lukas Meyer: Got it. Jan 31, 5pm CET. Portal upload. And there’s a bank-specific security questionnaire. Thanks.

[01:38] Lukas Meyer: On Redwood side we’ll coordinate a single response, but for security evidence there are some things we can share directly, and some under NDA. Olga will cover that.

[01:49] Olga Petrov: Hi everyone. Yeah, I can jump in once we understand what artifacts you’re expecting.

[01:55] Marie Keller: In general we need: SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test summary, data processing addendum template, list of subprocessors, and then answers to the questionnaire regarding retention, encryption, access controls, incident notification and so on.

[02:13] Marie Keller: For data residency, we need confirmation of EU-only processing and EU-only storage, including logs. This is not negotiable. Also we need to understand support access: where engineers are located and if remote access is possible.

[02:31] Lukas Meyer: Perfect. That’s exactly the stuff we’ve been getting in other RFPs too. We can address most in our security FAQ and the one-pagers, and we can supply SOC 2 report under NDA.

[02:43] Erik Jensen: We’ll also have questions about audit logs, SIEM export. We need to ingest events to Splunk.

[02:50] Tomasz Nowak: And networking. If we choose private, is it VPC, is it on-prem, what is the model update mechanism, what traffic egress exists, etc.

[03:02] Lukas Meyer: Great. Colin can cover the private architecture at a high level. And Fatima can cover deployment modes.

[03:09] Lukas Meyer: Before we go into technical, can we do a quick stakeholder map so we know who approves? Like security sign-off, risk sign-off, procurement, and timeline for review.

[03:20] Anna Bergström: Yes. Procurement collects it, and then we route: security will do the security questionnaire and evidence check. IT risk will check contractual and compliance points. Platform checks technical feasibility. Then we have a steering committee the first week of February.

[03:38] Lukas Meyer: Okay, so end Jan response, early Feb committee.

[03:43] Sven Richter: And architecture review is ongoing. We are comparing with three options: managed cloud services and two specialist vendors.

[03:51] Lukas Meyer: Understood. And just to level set, Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private deployment (VPC and also on-prem options in certain cases). But we are not going to promise features outside what exists today.

[04:07] Marie Keller: Good. We prefer clarity.

[04:10] Lukas Meyer: Cool. Let’s talk about the residency requirement because that’s usually the crux. Marie, when you say EU-only processing and storage, do you mean the inference requests, prompts, outputs, logs, and backups all must stay in the EU region? And also that there is no failover to the US.

[04:29] Marie Keller: Yes. Inference and any stored data. Logs as well, including operational logs. We can accept that some metadata exists, but we need it spelled out. And no cross-border transfer as a default.

[04:43] Erik Jensen: And if there is any remote admin access, we need controls: approvals, break-glass, logging, and ideally EU-based support personnel, but we can discuss.

[04:56] Fatima Noor: This is Fatima. So how we typically answer: by deployment mode.

[05:02] Fatima Noor: For Private in your VPC, the control boundary is simplest: your environment, your region, your network rules. Redwood components that run in your VPC process the data there. Support access is controlled by your policies.

[05:15] Fatima Noor: For Dedicated in our cloud account, we can provision in EU regions. Data plane stays in-region. We need to be careful with language about operational telemetry and incident response; we can align on what is collected, and how it’s stored, and how long.

[05:31] Fatima Noor: For Hosted API, we have EU regions as well, but the shared multi-tenant nature sometimes raises additional questions for banks. So we usually recommend Dedicated EU or Private VPC for regulated workloads.

[05:47] Tomasz Nowak: When you say EU region, which ones exactly? Frankfurt, Dublin, something else?

[05:53] Fatima Noor: It depends on the cloud provider region you choose. We can offer EU regions including Frankfurt and Dublin for dedicated, and for private it’s whatever region you deploy into. Lukas, we should confirm what Nordbank requires.

[06:08] Lukas Meyer: Yes, we’ll confirm region list in writing; we’ll avoid naming anything we can’t actually deliver.

[06:15] Colin O'Donnell: And for private VPC, just to add: we have a private control plane option where the customer has customer-managed networking. In practice that means you can isolate endpoints, do private link, restrict egress. We can talk details in the technical deep dive.

[06:33] Sven Richter: We will want diagrams. The RFP asks for data flow diagrams.

[06:38] Colin O'Donnell: We have a standard data flow diagram describing hosted vs dedicated vs private. It’s not super pretty, but it’s accurate.

[06:47] Lukas Meyer: Yeah, we can attach that. And we can keep it high-level.

[06:54] Olga Petrov: On evidence: SOC 2 report is available under NDA. We do not email it around broadly. We have an evidence request process where Anna or Marie can submit the request, confirm NDA, and we provide a secure link.

[07:09] Anna Bergström: We can do NDA. Do you provide your own or can we use ours?

[07:13] Olga Petrov: Usually we can use yours. We just need it executed before we share the full report.

[07:19] Marie Keller: Pen test summary?

[07:21] Olga Petrov: We can provide a pen test executive summary under NDA. For details, it depends. We’ll respond with approved language in the questionnaire.

[07:31] Erik Jensen: Okay.

[07:33] Lukas Meyer: On the questionnaire itself, is it an Excel workbook with many tabs? Or an online form.

[07:39] Anna Bergström: It’s an Excel workbook, yes. Several tabs, around 250 questions.

[07:44] Lukas Meyer: Cool. We have a response library for standard answers. We still need to review to make sure it maps cleanly.

[07:52] Marie Keller: Please do not copy-paste “ISO certified” language unless you are certified.

[07:57] Olga Petrov: Yes, agreed. We’re careful with ISO language. We can speak to alignment and controls, but we do not claim certification unless it’s true. We will use approved phrasing.

[08:10] Erik Jensen: Good.

[08:12] Lukas Meyer: Let’s hit a few high frequency areas so we know where we’ll have questions. Erik, you mentioned audit logs and Splunk.

[08:19] Erik Jensen: Yes. We need audit logging for admin actions, key events, user changes. If Redwood provides a console, we need to see log events. Also for API access, we want request-level logs.

[08:33] Colin O'Donnell: For the platform, audit logs cover identity and access events, configuration changes, and certain resource events. Export options are typically either streaming to an object store or a SIEM integration. The exact destinations we support vary; we should confirm whether Splunk HEC is needed or if you can ingest from S3.

[08:52] Tomasz Nowak: We can ingest from S3 to Splunk via our pipeline. But we need event format, schema, and retention.

[09:00] Colin O'Donnell: Makes sense. We have a taxonomy of events and fields. Some of this is in our docs. Some is in the internal product doc. We can provide a description in the RFP.

[09:11] Fatima Noor: Also depends on deployment mode. In Private VPC, you may be able to capture logs into your own logging stack directly, plus Redwood audit events.

[09:23] Marie Keller: On retention: We need customer content not retained or at least configurable. Prompts and outputs shouldn’t be stored beyond what’s needed for request processing.

[09:35] Lukas Meyer: Understood. Redwood’s default posture is not to use customer data for training without explicit agreement. On retention, we have specific controls and we need to describe them accurately per deployment mode. We’ll send the retention overview doc.

[09:49] Marie Keller: Please define “not used for training”. Some vendors mean they still store it.

[09:55] Olga Petrov: We can provide the formal wording. It generally means we do not use customer prompts/outputs to improve models unless the customer opts in via a separate agreement. Storage/retention is a separate control and we’ll document what we retain (e.g., logs) and for how long.

[10:12] Erik Jensen: Okay.

[10:14] Lukas Meyer: Another area: SSO and RBAC.

[10:17] Tomasz Nowak: Yes, we require SAML SSO and ideally SCIM for user provisioning. Also RBAC at least admin vs read-only vs billing, that kind of split.

[10:28] Colin O'Donnell: Redwood supports SSO via SAML for console access and has role-based access control. SCIM is supported for provisioning in enterprise tiers. We’ll need to note which features are available in which deployment mode and plan.

[10:44] Anna Bergström: Please include that in your response.

[10:47] Lukas Meyer: We will. And we’ll keep it consistent with our standard answers.

[10:51] Sven Richter: For private, do you run in Kubernetes? We have OpenShift.

[10:56] Colin O'Donnell: Typically yes, it’s a Kubernetes-based deployment. We can run on managed Kubernetes or customer-managed, depending. OpenShift can work but we’d need to validate version and constraints. This is probably for the deep dive.

[11:12] Lukas Meyer: Yeah let’s park the platform deep dive.

[11:15] Lukas Meyer: Switching back to evidence: DPA and subprocessors. Marie, do you need the full subprocessor list, including cloud providers.

[11:24] Marie Keller: Yes, and we need it to be current and include where they process data.

[11:29] Olga Petrov: We can provide a current subprocessor list under NDA or as part of the contractual pack. We also have standard DPA language. We’ll reference canonical documents rather than emailing old versions.

[11:42] Anna Bergström: Perfect.

[11:44] Lukas Meyer: Now, on EU residency: do you have any specific requirements about employee location? I heard “EU-based support” as a preference.

[11:52] Erik Jensen: It’s a control we look at. The key is that access is limited, logged, and approved. If data stays EU but a US engineer can access systems, we need to assess.

[12:06] Fatima Noor: For Private VPC, you can enforce that Redwood support has no standing access. We typically use time-bound, customer-approved access if needed. All actions are audited.

[12:18] Colin O'Donnell: For Dedicated, we can also use just-in-time access and audit logs for administrative actions. We’ll be careful not to oversell. Some operational functions may require Redwood to have access to manage the service, but it’s controlled.

[12:33] Marie Keller: We need that spelled out. Shared responsibility model.

[12:36] Lukas Meyer: Yep, we’ll include a shared responsibility section: what Redwood is responsible for vs what customer configures.

[12:45] Anna Bergström: Okay.

[12:47] Lukas Meyer: Let’s talk about the response plan so we hit your deadlines. We have a standard internal approval process for security language. That’s why we’d like the workbook as soon as possible.

[12:59] Anna Bergström: You’ll have it today. I can send after the call.

[13:03] Lukas Meyer: Great.

[13:05] Olga Petrov: Once we have the workbook, we can pre-fill a lot using our approved answers. Anything that deviates or asks for something we do not support, we’ll mark and propose alternative language.

[13:17] Marie Keller: Good.

[13:19] Lukas Meyer: Can you share which sections are most important to you? Like, what will be weighted.

[13:24] Anna Bergström: Data residency and security are the highest weight. Then performance and cost.

[13:30] Lukas Meyer: Makes sense.

[13:32] Tomasz Nowak: For performance, not today, but for security there is one question about “where are logs stored” and “how long retained.” We need exact numbers. Not “configurable” with no values.

[13:45] Colin O'Donnell: Understood. Some retention values are configurable, but there are also defaults. We’ll provide defaults and options. For example audit logs retention may be adjustable in enterprise plans; private you can align with your own retention.

[14:03] Lukas Meyer: We’ll respond with a table: default retention and configurable ranges, where applicable.

[14:09] Marie Keller: Also backup location.

[14:12] Fatima Noor: For private, backups are in your control. For dedicated, we can specify region and storage approach at a high level. We need to confirm exact behavior with engineering if needed, but again no promises.

[14:27] Erik Jensen: On incident response, we have a requirement: notification within 72 hours.

[14:33] Lukas Meyer: That’s typically contractual and reviewed by legal, but we can note our standard incident response process and that notification timelines are addressed in the contract. We’ll avoid making binding commitments in the questionnaire unless approved.

[14:49] Anna Bergström: Fine.

[14:51] Olga Petrov: We can provide a summary of our incident response program and reference SOC 2 controls.

[14:58] Lukas Meyer: Great.

[15:00] Lukas Meyer: Quick check: do you require HIPAA/BAA? Probably not, but I want to confirm.

[15:06] Marie Keller: No, not HIPAA. We’re a European bank.

[15:10] Lukas Meyer: Great.

[15:12] Sven Richter: We might have requirements around EBA guidelines, outsourcing register, etc.

[15:17] Fatima Noor: Okay. If you have specific regulatory questionnaires, send them. We can respond with our controls and shared responsibility. Sometimes there are “outsourcing” checklists that map to vendor governance.

[15:31] Lukas Meyer: We can coordinate that.

[15:34] Anna Bergström: The pack includes an “outsourcing appendix.” I’ll send it.

[15:38] Lukas Meyer: Perfect.

[15:40] (crosstalk)

[15:41] Lukas Meyer: Sorry, go ahead.

[15:43] Erik Jensen: One question: do you support customer-managed keys, like bring-your-own-key.

[15:48] Colin O'Donnell: We support encryption at rest and in transit. For key management: for private deployments, customers can integrate with their own KMS/HSM depending on environment. For dedicated, there are options; we need to respond carefully per mode and plan.

[16:05] Fatima Noor: It’s a frequent question. We will answer: at-rest encryption uses cloud KMS by default, and enterprise customers can request additional key management options. We will not claim full BYOK everywhere if not available.

[16:21] Marie Keller: We need clarity on that. If it is “roadmap” say so.

[16:26] Olga Petrov: We will not include roadmap commitments. We’ll state what’s available now.

[16:31] Lukas Meyer: Thanks.

[16:33] Tomasz Nowak: Also, do you have “no data leaves EU” guarantee even during outages? Like failover.

[16:40] Lukas Meyer: Great question. We can support region pinning so traffic stays in region. Cross-region failover is a policy choice, not automatic, and we can disable it for regulated workloads. We’ll document this in the response.

[16:56] Sven Richter: That’s important.

[16:59] Lukas Meyer: Okay.

[17:00] Lukas Meyer: Let’s align on what we’re sending you post-call. I propose: (1) enterprise security FAQ, (2) data residency & retention overview, (3) audit logging overview, (4) SSO/SCIM/RBAC capabilities summary, (5) evidence request instructions for SOC 2 under NDA.

[17:18] Anna Bergström: Sounds good.

[17:20] Marie Keller: Add subprocessor list and DPA link.

[17:23] Olga Petrov: We’ll provide where to request those. Some are gated.

[17:28] Lukas Meyer: Great.

[17:30] Lukas Meyer: Then for the RFP workbook, we’ll take first pass by mid next week, but I’d like to set expectations: there might be a few clarifying questions we send you quickly.

[17:42] Anna Bergström: That’s fine.

[17:44] Lukas Meyer: Then we schedule the private deep dive to answer Tomasz and Sven’s questions.

[17:49] Tomasz Nowak: Yes.

[17:50] Lukas Meyer: What days work next week? Wednesday or Thursday.

[17:55] Anna Bergström: Wednesday morning is okay.

[17:57] Tomasz Nowak: Wednesday 10:00 CET.

[18:00] Lukas Meyer: Great, we’ll send invite.

[18:03] Erik Jensen: I’ll join.

[18:05] Lukas Meyer: Perfect.

[18:07] (brief silence)

[18:09] Lukas Meyer: Any other high-risk items we should address now? Things that usually block bank procurement.

[18:16] Marie Keller: Data retention. Explicitly: do you store prompts/outputs for debugging?

[18:21] Fatima Noor: For hosted, some operational logging may include request metadata; the specifics are described in our retention overview. Customers can request reduced retention depending on plan. For dedicated and private, options are stricter. We’ll provide the accurate statement.

[18:39] Marie Keller: Okay.

[18:40] Erik Jensen: And vulnerability management. We ask about scanning frequency and third-party pentest frequency.

[18:47] Olga Petrov: We can answer that in the questionnaire with approved language. Typically we do ongoing vulnerability scanning and periodic third-party penetration tests. We’ll provide the latest summary available.

[19:01] Lukas Meyer: Great.

[19:03] Sven Richter: For private, how are updates delivered? Is there an agent, does Redwood pull images.

[19:09] Colin O'Donnell: Updates are delivered as container images and manifests via a secure distribution mechanism. In some deployments, customers pull from an approved registry; in others, we support offline transfer for restricted environments. We’ll discuss in deep dive. Not all options are available by default.

[19:27] Tomasz Nowak: Okay.

[19:29] Lukas Meyer: Great. I think we have enough for kickoff.

[19:33] Lukas Meyer: Let’s do recap and owners.

[19:36] Lukas Meyer: Anna will send the full RFP workbook and outsourcing appendix today. Olga will send the evidence request instructions and start NDA steps. Fatima and Colin will draft the deployment-mode language and data residency phrasing for the RFP. I’ll coordinate and send you a response plan email today.

[19:56] Anna Bergström: Yes.

[19:57] Marie Keller: Yes.

[19:59] Erik Jensen: Works.

[20:01] Lukas Meyer: Cool. Any last questions.

[20:04] (crosstalk)

[20:05] Tomasz Nowak: Not from me.

[20:07] Sven Richter: No.

[20:09] Lukas Meyer: Great. Thanks everyone.
